question: Haven — ATK, 2v3 down after a trade near B, no spike, 0:46 left. You (Harbor) still have Cascade, Cove and High Tide. How do you play the man-down round?

options.label: Group with your last teammate and commit one site behind Harbor's wall, not two solo duels
options.explication_courte: Down a man, you can't win two separate fights. Stack with your teammate, use Cascade/High Tide to block the defenders' sightlines, and take one site as a pair so every fight is a 2v1, not a 1v1.

sources_option.citation: Concentrate numbers and utility on a single approach; splitting a man-down attack lets defenders isolate and trade you one at a time

options.label: Split off solo through Mid to catch a rotating defender out of position
options.explication_courte: A lurk can win by catching a rotator, but going alone 2v3 means if you die first it's an unwinnable 1v3 for your teammate. Only split if you have a real timing read, not on hope.

sources_option.citation: A lurker's first job is to stay alive; dying alone early hands the round to the defense and strands your teammate

options.label: Dry-swing B main now to force a fast fight before defenders settle
options.explication_courte: Rushing a fight without your smokes down, a man short, throws away the one edge you still have — utility. You feed the defenders' crossfire on their terms instead of yours.

sources_option.citation: Taking space and executes should be backed by utility; dry-swinging into set defenders when down a player is low-percentage

options.label: Fully retreat and play for the clock / next round eco
options.explication_courte: With 46s and full utility in a 2v3 you still have a real chance to plant. Conceding the round outright wastes the tools you're holding and gives the defense a free win.

sources_option.citation: A 2v3 with time and utility remains winnable via a coordinated hit; timing the defenders' rotation beats conceding

explication_longue: A 2v3 down a man is not a lost round — but it is a round you can only win by concentrating force. The core error attackers make here is treating it like a normal round and drifting apart, which lets three defenders take two isolated 1v1s and win both. Harbor's kit is exactly what a man-down attack wants: Cascade and High Tide can wall off the defenders' angles so your pair enters a site with the fight cut down to a single line, turning every duel into a 2v1 on your terms. Grouping with your last teammate behind that water is the highest-EV line. A solo Mid lurk is defensible only with a genuine rotation read, because dying first makes it a 1v3; on a guess it just donates the round. Dry-swinging B with no smokes down burns your only remaining advantage — utility — by fighting on the defense's terms. And with 46 seconds plus full util still in your pocket, fully retreating throws away a live chance to plant. Down a man, you win by stacking bodies and util on one problem, not by spreading yourself across three.

sources.citation: Map-control fundamentals — concentrate numbers and utility to take space; coordinated execs beat scattered solo pushes
